opener_episode.title: How to Build and Scale a Category-Defining Firm Without Losing Culture
opener_episode.why: Freshest founder-scaling episode; 'category-defining' maps directly to Avery coining Click & Mortar and building one of the first online-only blue-chip galleries into an eight-figure business. Note: with a daily show, a personalized opener matters less than the application itself.

angles.headline: Click & Mortar: building an eight-figure art business online before collectors trusted it
angles.pitch: Avery's worst moment, biggest lesson and the playbook behind launching ArtLife.com in 2015 and pairing social-first marketing with physical pop-ups.
angles.builds_on: Nick Leopard (2026-10-02) on building a category-defining firm

angles.headline: Turning a street artist into a global brand
angles.pitch: How Avery developed Alec Monopoly from street art into sold-out exhibitions from New York to Morocco and major brand partnerships, and what any founder can steal from it.
angles.builds_on: Show's standard founder-journey format (e.g., DeBiase franchise episode, 2026-10-04)

angles.headline: Selling to the 1%: what celebrities and HNW clients really want
angles.pitch: Lessons in high-ticket sales and client service from advising celebrities, athletes and HNW collectors, including placing a $100K+ work with Kris Jenner at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024.
angles.builds_on: Show's practical sales/marketing episodes (e.g., Rachael Doukas, 2026-10-05)

booking.route: Official guest application on the show site (eofire.com/guest/, also eofire.com/apply/). Page states ~400-500 inquiries a month for 20-30 spots.

format: Daily episodes, ~20-40 min, tightly structured (worst entrepreneurial moment, biggest lesson, rapid-fire questions). Remote audio interviews; host based in Puerto Rico (earlier research). Guests: mostly small and mid-size founders, coaches and service-business owners. Guest gets a call-to-action, a show-notes page, newsletter inclusion and social promotion. Show claims ~1M+ monthly listens.
red_flags: PAY-TO-PLAY: search results tied to the eofire.com/guest page report a $3,500 appearance fee (current amount unverified; confirm before applying)
Daily volume means low per-episode prestige; mostly small-business guests
2023-era rumor the show was listed for sale (~$15M) on Website Closers; no confirmed sale; John Lee Dumas still named as host on the site
